clue.text: Ubiquitous, or kept within house limits?

definitions.meaning: found everywhere, covering every surface or space
read literally, something stretching from one wall of a room to the opposite one stays inside the house

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something pervasive, filling every available space, like fitted carpet from edge to edge.

clue.text: Printer's facility awarded compensation after internet's taken over

indicators.note: the compensation word follows the internet word, which in a down light is taken over it

parts.note: the web is the internet
an offset is something set off against a loss, a compensation

explanation.surface: A printing firm is paid damages after an online company takes it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' fits the down grid: WEB sits on top. Web offset is a printing process using continuous rolls of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Web offset is a lithographic printing method feeding a continuous roll, the facility of large printers.

clue.text: Poem in Latin? I cry for translation

indicators.note: to be translated, i.e. turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student weeps at having to turn a Latin verse into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for translation' rearranges L, I and CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling, originally sung to the lyre.

clue.text: It's hard to express just how tricky this is

definitions.text: It's hard to express just how tricky this is

parts.words: It's hard to express just how tricky this is
parts.note: seems to say something is indescribably difficult, but literally describes a phrase designed to be hard to say aloud

explanation.definitionFit: Such a phrase is built of similar sounds, so it is difficult to pronounce quickly.

clue.text: Somewhat lacklustre desire to cover English races

indicators.note: the first word is covering the others, so they go inside it

parts.note: to wish is to desire
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A half-hearted wish to report on England's race meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British slang for feeble or wimpish, which is why 'lacklustre' fits once '-ish' softens it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet in British usage means feeble or lacking spirit, and the suffix makes it 'rather' so.

clue.text: Co-operation — one of the signs top class is involved

indicators.note: the pieces are involved, i.e. wrapped up inside the sign

parts.note: Leo the lion is a sign of the zodiac
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
the contracted form of is gives S

explanation.surface: Joint working is said to be one of the hallmarks of an elite set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' gives only its contracted 's, as in 'top class's involved'; 'is involved' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a working link or co-operation between groups, as between departments.

clue.text: Old artist endlessly recycled

indicators.note: cycled back round, so the shortened name is read backwards
without its end, so the final letter of the painter's name is dropped

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: An elderly painter keeps going round in circles, reusing his material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the S from DEGAS to leave DEGA, and 'recycled' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone advanced in years is old; the two words are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Major stars offered spendid support

parts.note: great means splendid or excellent, the printed word being a typo for that
to bear is to support a weight

explanation.surface: Leading actors gave magnificent backing to a production.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'spendid', a typo for 'splendid'. The constellation is Ursa Major, Latin for great bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation Ursa Major, a group of stars, is also called by this English name.

clue.text: Doctor drinking whisky one's found in launderette

indicators.note: the doctor takes the spirit in, so it goes inside

parts.note: rye is an American whisky

explanation.surface: A medic tipples whisky while waiting for the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumble dryer is a machine found among the washers in a launderette.

clue.text: Peer I noticed in pub, tiddly to start with

indicators.note: something noticed in a place is seen inside it, so the word for I sits within the other letters

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word tiddly is wanted

parts.note: the numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone spots a nobleman slightly drunk in the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noticed in' reads as 'seen inside', the container signal. Strictly a baronet is not a peer, but setters often treat the hereditary titles loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary title ranking below a baron, loosely counted among the nobility.

clue.text: Be called back in to administer Cumbrian horse fair

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the other piece

parts.note: to apply a remedy or treatment is to administer it

indicators.note: a word called back is recalled, read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone is summoned back to run a horse fair in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called back' signals the reversal. Appleby in Cumbria holds a famous annual horse fair attended by Gypsy and Traveller communities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cumbrian town gives its name to the long-established gathering where horses are traded.

clue.text: Keep shaking, about to get cross, perhaps

definitions.text: Keep shaking, about to get cross, perhaps

parts.words: Keep shaking, about to get cross, perhaps
parts.note: seems to describe someone trembling with rising anger, but means going round shaking hands, as a politician does with the crowd

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to greet many people by shaking hands, typically a campaigning politician working a crowd.

clue.text: Shawl needed in a terrific hurry

indicators.note: what is needed in the phrase is found inside its run of letters, spanning two words

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a wrap as they dash out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed in' points inside 'terrific hurry', whose letters run on to spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a light triangular shawl or scarf worn about the neck and shoulders.

clue.text: What preceded Morse for transmission purposes?

definitions.text: What preceded Morse for transmission purposes?

parts.words: What preceded Morse for transmission purposes?
parts.note: seems to ask about telegraphy before Morse code, but means the rank that came before the detective's surname in the title of the television series

explanation.definitionFit: The TV drama starring John Thaw was titled with the detective's police rank placed before his surname.

clue.text: Appear preplexed, having problem with locks?

definitions.meaning: to look puzzled, as printed with the setter's spelling of perplexed
locks are hair, so an itchy scalp would make someone do this literally

explanation.definitionFit: The gesture of rubbing the scalp is the stock sign of puzzlement, so the idiom means looking baffled.

clue.text: A sign worker's in work regularly, with a vengeance!

parts.note: Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: the worker sits inside the other piece

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily
an ant is the classic worker insect; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An astrologer's labourer toils steadily and with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the surprising definition: 'with a vengeance' is an adverbial phrase, matching the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something rampantly is doing it unrestrainedly and violently, which is to do it with a vengeance.

clue.text: Time set aside for steady revision

indicators.note: revising something changes it, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone books off a period for steady study before exams.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of rest is a period kept free from work, such as the Sabbath.

clue.text: Three men in the street

parts.note: plays on the idiom of the man in the street, an ordinary person, multiplied by three into the stock trio of common names

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names three generic ordinary men, standing for anyone at all, everyday folk.

clue.text: Withdrawing normal parking allowed for minor dignitary

indicators.note: the standard word is withdrawn, i.e. taken out of the word parking

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Ordinary parking privileges are removed and given to a petty official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'normal' looks like an adjective on 'parking', but is the golf term for the standard score; 'Withdrawing' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinglet is a petty or minor king, the diminutive suffix making him a lesser dignitary.

clue.text: New variant almost developed into perfect state

indicators.note: the letters are developed into something else, rearranged
almost all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A new strain of a virus has nearly evolved into perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts VARIANT to VARIAN; 'developed into' rearranges N plus VARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism nirvana is the perfect state of release from suffering and desire.

clue.text: Disciplinarian has brought in recent innovation

indicators.note: the other word is brought inside, so the rearranged letters surround it
an innovation is a making new, so the letters of the word recent are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A strict teacher has introduced a new policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innovation' makes CTENER from the word recent; 'brought in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chastens corrects or punishes others, which is the role of a disciplinarian.

clue.text: Sweet, but extremely coy, perhaps?

parts.note: the extremes of the word coy are its first and last letters, which spoken as a pair become a phrase of three words

explanation.surface: A sweet thing but a very bashful one.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of 'coy' are C and Y; say 'C and Y' together and you have the answer. 'perhaps' flags the punning reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets and confectionery.

clue.text: Nap may be a mistake

definitions.meaning: the soft raised surface or fuzz on cloth
a blunder, especially a fumbled line or shot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the downy fibres on fabric and a bungled attempt, as when an actor muddles a line.

clue.text: Edict passed in this country when allied with Spain

parts.note: for a British newspaper, this country is the United Kingdom
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A law passed in Britain when it joined forces with Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A ukase was a decree of the Russian tsar, hence any arbitrary order.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was a tsarist decree, so by extension any edict or proclamation.

clue.text: An ideal person to be spontaneous

definitions.meaning: someone perfectly suited to a role, born to it

explanation.surface: Someone perfectly suited to acting off the cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A person ideally suited is a born talent, and unaffected behaviour is described with the same adjective.

clue.text: Mean to make assertion ahead of time

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the second

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly or assert
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to speak up before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the average, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: One or two playthings recalled, both wasting time?

indicators.note: there are two playthings, so the trimmed piece appears twice
wasting something loses it, so the letter for time is dropped
called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a toy is a plaything; the plural here covers the pair

explanation.surface: A child gets back a couple of old toys and both just pass the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns TOY into YOT; 'wasting' drops T (time) to leave YO; 'two' and 'both' make it YO twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is itself a single plaything, a spool spun up and down on a string.

clue.text: Affection that's communicated via e-mail

definitions.meaning: a file sent along with an electronic message

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an emotional bond to someone and a file sent along with an electronic message.
